01 Verdict

Official Apr–Jul is €875k vs €1,017k (−14%). Apr–Jun on that same cut is €644k vs €644k — flat. July is €231k vs €373k (−€142k) — that is the entire miss. This July is not in the billing file, so it cannot be split. Last July was 78% warranty.
Calendar-year totals look stable at ~€3.3m. They are not. The commercial book fell −59% in two years (€2.28m → €1.32m → €0.94m) while warranty grew to 56.5% of the year. That is the study. Credit notes are not sales and are not in these mix figures.

02 Which AIM families moved in this window

AIM is the Aftermarket Intelligence Model — the family grouping used for the rest of this page. Pale bar = last year. Terracotta = this year. Shell lubricants stay their own class. Hide warranty strips DPD / warranty PNs out of the family bars — Exhaust is mostly that. Default is hidden so you see the commercial book first.

04 Service-part capture — above or below the network

This is not one race. Each family is its own comparison: UMI total capture versus the rest of the network on that same family (this distributor is not in the network bar). Navy = UMI. Grey = network. The left list is above. The right list is below. Complete calendar 2025 only. Primary capture is total (genuine + BVP), not genuine-only.

Above the network

UMI capture is higher than the network on this family.

Below the network

UMI capture is lower than the network on this family.

Oil filter sits above because BVP units do the work (genuine-only is much lower). Pads, rotors, air and fuel sit below — that is the euro gap. Apr–Jun service-basket billing is up versus last year; the capture hole is structural, not this quarter’s cliff.

05 GPS — commercial first

Headline is GPS excluding warranty (the commercial book) at 18,349 × €250. The dashed line includes warranty — that is the contractual lens, and with warranty at 56% of the year it mostly tracks warranty. Live FY2027 rate €262.50 is its own chip, not mixed into the three-year trend.

06 Part numbers — still selling, lost volume

Default is live lines: sold last year and still selling this year, but less. That is the repeat-buy drop, not one-shot turbos and body that did not come back. Terracotta = quantity effect (last year’s unit price × change in units). Navy = price effect (this year’s unit price minus last year’s, × this year’s units). If this year sold zero units, price effect is €0 by definition — those sit under Did not repeat. SPA watch is Special Price Agreement candidates from our billing (wear still moving, units down). UMI still owes the PN / 12-month qty / target prices. Default hides Shell lubricants and warranty.

07 Same book — and what is still open

Sales-to-dealer at part level from January 2025 is still with UMI. Without it we see ISZE billing, not what left their warehouse. Fill rate is not on file.
July is the whole official miss and it is not in this billing file. Last July was 78% warranty; this July cannot be split until that month lands.

Sources: official Apr–Jul sales cut (locked 12 Aug 2026); ISZE billing for this distributor only; credit notes are not sales; complete-year service-parts capture versus the rest of the network; GPS on this study’s billed € and 18,349 × €250. Not a customer CSV. Not another Israel distributor.
